newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Limited intervention to guide market - Manila cbank.
newsitem.headline: Limited intervention to guide market - Manila cbank.

text.p: The Philippine central bank said on Tuesday its limited intervention in foreign exchange markets was necessary to provide direction to an aimless market.

"Essentially, it is to provide direction to the market, some indicative guidance," central bank managing director Amado Tetangco told reporters when asked why the bank had been selling dollars at 29.00.
The peso has closed at the 29.00 level since Monday with help from central bank intervention.
The central bank has been selling dollars on a very limited scale, despite its announcement on Friday that it was allowing the peso to float in a wider range.
The peso fell as low as 30 pesos to the dollar on Tuesday, sharply down from Thursday's close of 26.40, before recovering amid light turnover.
Traders said banks remained cautious as to the direction of the peso-dollar exchange rate.
Tetangco said the central bank would not show its hand in the early part of the session as it used to but would only enter the market in the afternoon.
"We are reviewing this (strategy) on a continuing basis, and we will adopt measures that are necessary," Tetangco said when asked if the strategy would persist in the coming days.
